Ecobank Transnational Incorporated (ETI), the parent company of Ecobank Group, has announced the exit of three members of its board of directors.
The bank disclosed this in a statement, signed by Madibinet Cisse, the company secretary, and issued in Lomé, Togo, on Tuesday.
The departing directors are David O’Sullivan, a Non-Executive Director nominated by Qatar National Bank; Zanele Monnakgotla, a Non-Executive Director nominated by Public Investment Corporation; and Esther Chibesa, an Independent Director.
Mr O’Sullivan and Ms Monnakgotla retired from the board after their respective tenures ended, while Ms Chibesa resigned to pursue other interests.
“The Board, Management and staff of ETI thank the departing Directors for their valuable contributions to the Ecobank Group and for their continued willingness to support the Group whenever called upon,” the statement said.
David O’Sullivan joined Ecobank Transnational Incorporated’s board in 2017. He has held several positions in the financial and legal sectors, including Head of Group Legal at Qatar National Bank and Director at Gulf Investment Corporation between 2006 and 2012.

He also worked as an Associate Director at HSBC Corporate Finance (Asia) between 2003 and 2006 and as a Senior Associate at Clifford Chance from 1996 to 2003. He graduated from Trinity College Dublin.
Moreover, Ms Monnakgotla has served on the boards of several organisations, including Sasol Khanyisa Public, Sasol South Africa, Rand Water and Adowa Properties.
She previously served on the boards of the Development Bank of Southern Africa, Philafrica Foods, the Small Enterprise Development Agency and the South African Bureau of Standards.
She also held senior management positions at the Industrial Development Corporation, where she served as Head of Innovation and Head of Strategic High Projects. She later founded Freewi Technologies, where she served as managing director.
Also, Ms Chibesa is a pan-African banking executive and board director with 25 years of experience leading and governing financial institutions across Sub-Saharan Africa.
She previously served as Non-Executive Director at Citibank Nigeria, where she chaired the Board Risk Management Committee and served on the Audit Committee.
As Managing Director for Citi Treasury and Trade Solutions across Sub-Saharan Africa until 2024, she led regional businesses spanning payments, digital channels, liquidity, trade finance and regulatory engagement across frontier and emerging markets.
Ecobank Group operates in 34 sub-Saharan African countries, as well as France, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates and China, providing consumer, commercial, corporate and investment banking services to over 30 million customers.
